title: Usage grain notes and feature snippets (working)
text:
Usage grain notes and feature snippets (working)

Purpose: quick consolidation of recent customer threads that share a similar usage grain (short chat sessions where 3rd-party tool calling + embeddings are mixed), plus compact feature snippets and low-risk fixes we can try in the next 2 sprints. This is intentionally light — sketch-level with prioritized next steps and suggested owner(s).

Summary Observations (fast bullets):
- Multiple customers (mid-market and one enterprise fintech) report short-lived sessions (~3–7 turns) with occasional spikes of identical prompts across users. Net effect: wasted tokens, cold KV cache misses, and occasional latency spikes when requests land on a non-cached shard.
- Common ask: "Can we reuse cached prefixes across sessions for the same user or account?" Customers want a safe, opt-in prefix reuse/cache-hint that preserves privacy controls.
- Another pattern: many customers are sending small tool-call wrappers inside messages which inflate token counts but are identical across calls (e.g., metadata wrappers, JSON envelopes).
- Recurrent ask: clearer guidance and defaults for batching thresholds — customers are unsure how to pick batch size vs latency tradeoffs for bursty small sessions.

Representative customer quotes (paraphrased):
- "We see 30–40% repeated boilerplate in requests — if we could dedupe that server-side we'd save a ton." — SMB analytics startup.
- "Our LLM costs jump at month-end because a surge of short report requests all repeat the same prefix." — enterprise finance team.

Feature snippets and quick patches (ranked by expected impact / effort):
1) Prefix-cluster cache hint (low effort, small infra lift) — allow client to mark a prefix as reusable with an account-scoped cache token. Safety: token TTL + optional ACL label. Developer note: MVP stores hashed prefix -> KV key, not raw text; expose metrics to track reuse. Owner: eng-serving-runtime + product. Expected upside: 15–25% token reduction for impacted workflows.

2) Server-side envelope dedupe (small effort) — detect identical outer JSON envelopes up to N bytes and strip before tokenization when sender opts in. Risk: must preserve signatures/hmac ordering; add audit log. Owner: devex + runtime. Upside: reduces billable tokens per request without changing model outputs.

3) Batch-config wizard in Console (medium effort) — interactive tool that analyzes a customer's request size distribution and recommends batch/window params. Include "simulated cost" slider. Owner: product-console + optimize. Upside: faster onboarding and fewer manual support threads.

4) Fast-fallback routing for small bursts (medium effort) — route <100-token requests to an ultra-low-latency small-instance pool with cheaper quantized model; fallback to main pool if mismatch. Owner: platform-routing + infra. Upside: lower p95 latency and lower unit cost for burst traffic.

Quick experiments we can run this sprint (7–14 days):
- A/B: apply simple envelope dedupe on 10 pilot accounts (CS identifies candidates). Track token reduction, error rates, and customer feedback. Metric: tokens_per_session drop and any change in perplexity/quality.
- Telemetry: add prefix-hit label to existing request logs for a handful of customers (no payload capture) so we can estimate theoretical reuse without enabling cache. Metric: estimated_reusable_token_pct.
- Console microflow: prototype batch-config wizard mock in Figma and run 3 customer interviews.

Risks and unknowns (notes-to-self):
- Privacy/regulatory: prefix reuse must not enable cross-account leakage. Need legal sign-off for account-scoped caching; consider customer-managed encryption keys if requested by enterprise.
- Complexity: storing hashed prefixes at scale could increase index cardinality; quantify storage + lookup cost before committing.
- Behavioral: customers might misuse cache hints leading to inconsistent outputs if prefixes include dynamic data (timestamps, ephemeral IDs). Need validation rules and SDK helpers.

Suggested metrics to add / dashboards:
- prefix_reuse_rate_by_account (daily), tokens_saved_estimate, envelope_dedupe_rate, p95_latency_by_pool (pre/post experiment), batch_window_utilization.

Suggested immediate owners and next steps (this doc is for handoff):
- Priya (CS) — coordinate pilot customers + capture ROI anecdotes (blocks: legal + account permissions).
- Ethan (Eng-serving-runtime) — spike on hashed-prefix store design (3 days) and rough cost estimate.
- Mariana (Product) — scope batch-config mock and embed simulated cost slider.
- Liam (DevEx) — prototype SDK helper to mark reusable prefix + validation checks.

Open questions for leadership review:
- Do we want cache-API to be available on Hosted by default or an opt-in beta only? Recommendation: beta opt-in for first 6 months.
- Tolerance for stale prefixes: what TTL targets do we want (30m / 24h / 7d)? Suggest 24h default with customer override.

Appendix: pilot candidate criteria (CS use):
- >50k tokens/mo, majority short sessions, willingness to opt-in to beta, legal ok with hashed prefix telemetry.

Slack refs / quick links: #cs-field-notes thread pinned 2026-11-28, thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345678/p1748
Jira spikes to create: ENG-1282 (hashed-prefix store spike), FEAT-237 (console wizard), CS-5420 (pilot onboarding).

Notes: this is intentionally informal; collect customer IDs offline and attach to pilot signup form. Will convert to a more formal brief if leadership greenlights the beta.
